item.title: [LU-8622] recovery-small test_24b: no discarded dirty page found!
item.description:

I am not pretty sure if this is test issue or not, error_ignore call means test results to be ignored, but then second check for 'discard' message makes test FAIL. It looks like we don't need to check for 'discard' after error_ignore() call or why to have that error_ignore() at all?

On other side, I am not sure what test expect to check, there are two processes, one sleeps on 'fsync', another on 'close'.  Both should fail after eviction, so there should be two messages about "dirty page discard:", but test doesn't check that, it passes if single one exists.

I've checked several runs and find that:

recovery-small test_24b: @@@@@@ IGNORE (bz5494): multiop didn't fail fsync: 5 or close: 0 

note, in some cases there are two 'discard' messages for 'fsync' and 'close' (-5 and -108) but also there a lot more cases when only one 'discard' message occurred with -108 error (for close only?). It looks like in half cases fsync failure doesn't produce 'discard' message and that is just not noticed because test doesn't check that, so in all cases only 'discard' message from close let test pass and test fails if 'close' is not failed after eviction for some reason.

So we need more expertise here to answer these questions:

  • should fsync failure produce 'discard' message or not? If not necessary, then why 'fsync' test is there?
  • should test check always for two 'discard'  messages if both writes failed?
  • should test result be ignored if one of writes doesn't fail and skip check for 'discard'? Or it need to be more robust and check for as many 'discard' and failed writes

Could the lack of ll_dirty_page_discard_warn() messages be caused by rate limiting of console error messages? We've had similar kinds of failures in other tests, especially if they are run in a loop. Rather than checking the console logs, it would be more robust to dump the debug logs and check for the message there, IFF the debug logs are large enough (i.e. the test itself is not so complex that the message has aged out of the debug log).

doesn't look so, here is an example of console log from repeated run of 24b:

https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_logs/d1675a74-95b2-4656-b5d0-a710ab7bddf9/show_text

test page: https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/bce221d2-6abc-4ba3-acce-829f1cbb8d15

It has no rate limiting messages when single page discard occurred

The rate limiting message is only printed after the rate limiting has finished and the next time the message is printed again.

That said, I looked through the debug log for the failed subtest and didn't see any dirty page discard message either. Is it possible that the page is already written by the time the client is evicted?
